title: System design roadmap
summary: A learning path through the core building blocks of scalable systems. Each topic builds on the one before it. Only Caching is written so far; click it to start.

nodes.label: Caching
nodes.what: Keep copies of hot data in fast memory so most reads never reach the database.
nodes.why: It is the cheapest way to cut latency and database load, and it introduces the central trade-off of the field: speed versus freshness.
nodes.gotcha: Invalidation. Reading through a cache is easy; keeping it correct after writes is the hard part.

nodes.label: Load balancing
nodes.what: Spread requests across many identical servers and route around the dead ones.
nodes.why: One server is a capacity limit and a single point of failure. A balancer turns many servers into one service.
nodes.gotcha: Stateless servers scale easily; sticky sessions and in-memory state quietly break that.

nodes.label: Databases & replication
nodes.what: Copy the database to replicas for read scale and failover.
nodes.why: Caching only goes so far; the source of truth must itself survive a machine loss and serve more reads.
nodes.gotcha: Replicas lag. A read right after a write can return old data.

nodes.label: Sharding
nodes.what: Split data across machines by a key so no single node holds it all.
nodes.why: Replication scales reads; sharding is how you scale writes and total data size.
nodes.gotcha: The shard key decides everything. A bad one gives hot shards and painful cross-shard queries.

nodes.label: Queues & async
nodes.what: Hand slow or bursty work to a queue and let workers process it at their own pace.
nodes.why: It decouples producers from consumers, absorbs spikes and lets a request return before the work is done.
nodes.gotcha: Delivery is usually at-least-once, so consumers must be idempotent.

nodes.label: CDNs
nodes.what: Serve static and cacheable content from edge servers close to users.
nodes.why: Distance is latency. A CDN is caching applied geographically.
nodes.gotcha: Purging a CDN is slow and global; version your asset URLs instead.

nodes.label: Consistency & CAP
nodes.what: What every replica sees, and when, once data lives in more than one place.
nodes.why: Caches, replicas and shards all trade consistency for speed or availability. This names the trade.
nodes.gotcha: CAP is about behavior during a network partition, not a menu of two-out-of-three at all times.

nodes.label: Rate limiting
nodes.what: Cap how many requests a client can make in a time window.
nodes.why: It protects shared capacity from abuse, bugs and retry storms.
nodes.gotcha: Limits kept per server instead of in shared state let a client multiply its quota by the server count.

flows.title: How to use this roadmap
flows.summary: Follow the arrows; open a topic to read it and play its flows.

steps.title: Start with Caching
steps.does: Click the box to open the Caching folder. Read the page, then switch to the Map tab.
steps.note: Boxes with a link open; the rest are planned.

steps.title: Follow the arrows
steps.does: Each topic leans on the one before it. Caching creates the need for consistency thinking; load balancing and replication create the need to scale.

steps.title: Return to the hard parts
steps.does: Consistency & CAP names the trade-offs you already met in caching. Come back to it once you have seen replicas and shards.
